problem: LSP/ISP: ReviewAgentAdapter.cancel is optional precisely so an adapter that cannot cancel omits it, yet the recorded adapter implements it as a method that always throws 'not supported' (and simultaneously advertises capabilities.cancellation: false at line 97). The sibling in the same change, cancelPendingDispatches (adapter-shutdown.ts:50-54), decides support by `adapter.cancel === undefined`, so it treats this adapter as cancellable and awaits a guaranteed rejection with no try/catch. Sites: recorded-adapter.ts:113-114 (throwing stub), adapter-shutdown.ts:50 (presence check), adapter-shutdown.ts:54 (unguarded await); enumeration: keryx ctx rg for `adapter?.cancel` / `.cancel(` under src/review/agents — controller.ts:422 is the only other caller and it catches.
impact: A host shutting down a run with any recorded dispatch pending gets a rejected promise from cancelPendingDispatches: the loop stops at that dispatch, later dispatches on real adapters are never asked to stop (the provider work the module exists to stop keeps running), and no AdapterShutdownReport is returned. Omitting cancel would put the dispatch in `skipped` as intended.

problem: Disguised failure (error-handling.mdc Rule 1 / Iron Law 2; it is the rule's own BAD example): loadRecordedResults swallows a missing file, an unreadable file and malformed JSON into `null`, and its only caller turns that into an empty recording (`?? []`, line 83). execute then answers every dispatch with `{ findings: [] }` (line 108-109), which is indistinguishable from a recorded run that found nothing except for a metadata flag.
impact: A typo in recordingPath or a corrupt recording makes a dry run / plan-eval replay complete 'successfully' with zero findings for every task; whoever reads the replay concludes the plan produced a clean review instead of learning the recording was never read.

problem: Hidden side effect / output argument: isReplayableResult is documented and named as a predicate but sorts entry.scopeIds in place, and RecordedEntry.scopeIds (line 24) was made the one mutable field to allow it. scopesMatch (line 72-74) silently depends on that mutation having happened, since it compares a sorted request against entry.scopeIds index by index.
impact: Anyone calling scopesMatch on an entry that did not pass through isReplayableResult (or reordering the filter) gets false mismatches with no visible reason; the next editor of either function has to discover the coupling by debugging.

problem: Magic number duplicated: the replay staleness window `7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` is written inline twice, once deciding replayability and once deciding `stale` in the summary (line 151), with no named constant tying the two together.
impact: Changing the window in one place makes the summary call entries stale that the adapter still replays (or the reverse), and the number's meaning has to be reconstructed by the reader.

problem: Comment does not match the code under it: it says the empty reply is for 'a task the recorded run never reached' and that 'the summary counts it', but the branch also covers entity and scope mismatches of tasks that were recorded, and writeReplaySummary (line 129) summarises the recording file only; nothing in the change reads `metadata.recorded`.
impact: A reader trusts that mismatched replays are counted somewhere and that the fallback only covers unreached tasks; neither holds, so mismatches go unnoticed.
quote: // `recorded: false`, so the replayed plan still completes and the summary counts it.

problem: Two readers of the same recording file with different contracts: writeReplaySummary (line 129-155) validates taskId, attempt and createdAt and throws with the path in the message, while loadRecordedResults casts the parsed array unvalidated. A missing scopeIds makes `[...stored.scopeIds]` throw a bare TypeError with no path or entry context (error-handling.mdc Rule 2), and other bad fields flow through silently.
impact: The same malformed recording fails loudly and explainably in the summary but either crashes without context or replays wrong data in the adapter; the validation has to be kept in sync by hand.

problem: Single-letter name compensated by a comment: `n` needs a trailing comment to say what it counts, and the value it holds is returned as `confirmed`.
impact: The comment exists only to explain a name; `confirmed` would make both the comment and the reader's lookup unnecessary.

problem: Third hand-written copy of the assignment status partition: RUNNING_STATUSES is the complement of the TERMINAL sets already defined in controller.ts:13 and store.ts:24, with no shared source tying them to ReviewAgentAssignmentStatus.
impact: Adding a status to ReviewAgentAssignmentStatus now requires updating three sets; missing this one makes pendingDispatches skip (or wrongly include) dispatches at shutdown.

impact: Call sites read `cancelPendingDispatches(a, p, x, y)` and can swap runId and reason without a type error.
